..
Issued at 257 AM EDT Tue Sep 15 2026

Today-Tonight... A surface front extending over the western Atlantic 
and through portions of the southeast U.S. early today is pushed 
further east-southeastward as high pressure expands along the 
eastern seaboard. Deep moisture persists across central Florida, 
south of the surface boundary. East-northeast onshore winds begin to 
increase 10-15 mph this afternoon as the local pressure gradient 
begins to tighten. Showers and storms over the local Atlantic early 
in the day should occasionally push onshore. A diffuse sea breeze 
looks to develop late morning and the into early afternoon bringing 
the greatest chances (50-60%) for showers and storms inland, west of 
I-95, after 12PM. Inland activity diminishes into early evening, 
while isolated to scattered rounds of showers and storms should 
continue along the coast through the overnight. Poor lapse rates 
should generally limit organized stronger storms today. However, 
increasing background flow and winds aloft could still allow for 
developing convection to produce wind gusts 40-50 mph. Otherwise, 
hazards remain occasional to frequent lightning strikes and locally 
heavy downpours. Afternoon temperatures will be seasonal around the 
upper 80s and low 90s, but humid conditions will still produce peak 
heat index values in the low triple digits (100-107F). Overnight low 
temperatures will mostly range the mid to upper 70s, remaining 
warmest along the coast. 

Wednesday-Thursday... Continued tightening of the local pressure 
gradient will further increase onshore flow to around 15-20+ mph 
Wednesday with peak gusts 25-30 mph at times. This will prompt a 
period of poor to hazardous beach and boating conditions, and a high
risk of life threatening rip currents along with rough surf is 
expected at all local beaches. East-northeast winds diminish to 
10-15 mph Thursday, remaining breezy, and a high risk of rip 
currents is expected to continue. Heed the advice of lifeguards, 
beach patrol flags, and signs. Entering the surf is not advised!

A drier airmass advects across central Florida on Wednesday with a 
tight moisture gradient extended southward through Lake Okeechobee. 
The PoP forecast mostly reflects this showing lower rain chances 
north of the Orlando Metro within the area of driest air. However, 
moistening of the lower levels within increased onshore flow should 
still allow for slight rain chances along the Volusia and northern 
Brevard Coast, and can't rule out a few of these showers sneaking 
further inland. Otherwise, deeper moisture south should allow for
rounds of scattered to numerous showers and a few storms 
throughout the day, continuing along the coast into Wednesday 
night.

Some slight adjustments have been made to the forecast into Thursday 
as a mid to upper level trough over the western Atlantic approaches 
Florida. Of note, some model guidance has slowed the westward 
progression of this feature. These slower solutions hold onto the
drier airmass across portions of north-central Florida longer 
than some of the previous forecast cycles. Therefore, rain chances
Thursday may look more similar to what is forecast Wednesday 
favoring continued rounds of scattered to numerous showers and a 
few storms across the south with lower rain chances north, 
especially northwest of I-4. 

High temperatures are forecast near normal Wednesday and Thursday, 
mostly reaching the upper 80s and near 90s degrees. Morning lows in 
the 70s will be highest along the coast. Areas along the Barrier 
Islands may struggle to fall below the 80 degree mark each morning.  

Friday-Monday... An unsettled pattern is forecast late week and into 
early next week as the mid to upper level trough passes over Florida 
and into the Gulf. Moisture recovers behind the trough, expanding
moderate to high rain chances more areawide. Light easterly winds
veer southeast to south late in the weekend, becoming locally 
enhanced onshore as a weak sea breeze develops each day. Afternoon
temperatures continue to hold near normal in the upper 80s and 
close to 90s degrees.
